% Pattern: structure/alias. A command of one argument opens the lemma
% environment and labels it with the argument through a label command, and a
% control symbol stands for \end, so \lemm{a} ... \>{lem} is lemma 1.1 with
% the label a, and the proof after it proves it. Seen in the gold pilot
% (set X).
% want lem-1 statement/lemma 1.1 status=here labels=a
% want proof-1 proof - proves=lem-1
% want lem-2 statement/lemma 1.2 status=none labels=b
\documentclass{article}
\newtheorem{lem}{Lemma}[section]
\def\lbl#1{ \label{#1}}
\def\>{\end}
\def\lemm#1{ \begin{lem} \lbl{#1} }
\def\prf{\begin{proof}}
\begin{document}
\section{One}
\lemm{a}
Every compact space is bounded.
\>{lem}
\prf
Cover the space by balls.
\end{proof}
\begin{lem}\label{b} Every finite space is compact. \end{lem}
\end{document}
